title: Finite-inertia stacks have stabilizer-preserving finite-flat affine charts
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $k$. Suppose $I_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal X$ is finite, where $I_{\mathcal X}(T)$ consists of pairs $(x,\alpha)$ with $x\in\mathcal X(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(x)$. Finiteness means that every scheme base change is a finite scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. There are a small set $J$ and algebraic stacks $\mathcal X_j/k$, with jointly surjective morphisms $g_j:\mathcal X_j\to\mathcal X$, such that each $g_j$ is representable by algebraic spaces, separated and etale, and induces an isomorphism $I_{\mathcal X_j}\simeq\mathcal X_j\times_{\mathcal X}I_{\mathcal X}$. Here etale is tested on scheme charts [def-weil-etale-morphism] and separated for a stack morphism means proper relative diagonal, using properness on scheme charts [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Each $\mathcal X_j$ has a representable surjective finite flat finitely presented map $U_j\to\mathcal X_j$ from an affine scheme. In particular $R_j=U_j\times_{\mathcal X_j}U_j$ is affine, its two projections to $U_j$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and $\mathcal X_j\simeq[U_j/R_j]$. No Deligne--Mumford or smooth-inertia hypothesis is imposed. Algebraic stacks and quasi-coherent sheaves have the meanings in [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space], and algebraic spaces have the meaning in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A 2-fibre product retains the specified isomorphism between the two images of an object. For an affine groupoid $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$, the groupoid laws are those of [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]; $[U/R]$ denotes the fppf stackification of the groupoid with objects $U(T)$ and arrows $R(T)$ on test schemes $T$.

proof.text: Fix $x\in|\mathcal X|$. Apply the pointwise chart theorem to obtain $h:\mathcal V=[U/R]\to\mathcal X$ and $v\mapsto x$, with $U,R$ affine, $s,t$ finite locally free and the stabilizer group schemes identified at $v$. This input applies to finite inertia itself; it requires neither a Deligne--Mumford hypothesis nor smooth inertia.

Apply the open-locus theorem to $h$. Its finite-inertia etale special case gives an open substack $\mathcal V^\circ\subseteq\mathcal V$ containing $v$ on which $I_{\mathcal V^\circ}\simeq\mathcal V^\circ\times_{\mathcal X}I_{\mathcal X}$. Pull it back to the invariant open $U^\circ\subseteq U$ using the flat-groupoid presentation theorem, and lift $v$ to a point $u\in U^\circ$. The whole orbit $E=t(s^{-1}(\{u\}))$ lies in $U^\circ$. It is finite because the finite map $s$ has finite fibres.

source.place: Tag 0DUE (lemma-etale-local-finite-inertia), second sentence and choice of u′

proof.text: Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. View it as $\operatorname{Proj}A[T]$ with $T$ of degree one: all homogeneous primes avoid $T$, and the sole chart $D_+(T)$ has degree-zero coordinate ring $A$. Thus $U^\circ$ is an open subscheme of this Proj. Apply the locally-closed-Proj finite-set lemma with $X=O=U^\circ$ and identity closed immersion to find an affine open in $U^\circ$ containing $E$. Apply the invariant-affine lemma to the restricted groupoid on $U^\circ$ to obtain an invariant affine open $W$ containing $E$. Its restricted arrow scheme is $R_W=s^{-1}(W)=t^{-1}(W)$; its projections are finite locally free by the presentation theorem.

source.place: Tag 0DUE (lemma-etale-local-finite-inertia), invariant affine shrinking, Tags 01ZY and 03JE

proof.text: Set $\mathcal X_x=[W/R_W]$. The quotient-open theorem identifies it with an open substack of $\mathcal V^\circ$ containing $v$, and supplies the representable surjective finite flat finitely presented map $W\to\mathcal X_x$. The composite $g_x:\mathcal X_x\to\mathcal X$ is representable etale by restricting $h$. Restricting the inertia isomorphism preserves it: an open substack is full, so the automorphism sheaf of any object in it is unchanged. Thus $g_x$ preserves inertia. Since $R_W\to W$ is finite and $W$ affine, $R_W$ is affine; it is canonically $W\times_{\mathcal X_x}W$.

source.place: Tag 0DUE (lemma-etale-local-finite-inertia), construction of the open quotient and its finite-flat affine cover

proof.text: The finite-flat affine groupoid diagonal theorem makes $\mathcal X_x$ separated over $k$. Apply separated-source cancellation with target $\mathcal X$, whose inertia is finite, to conclude that $g_x$ is separated. This checks relative separatedness; no separatedness of $\mathcal X$ over $k$ is assumed.

Take one such choice for each $x\in|\mathcal X|$ and let $J=|\mathcal X|$, a small set in the stipulated universes. Each $g_x$ has a point over $x$, so the family is jointly surjective. The finite flat presentations, affine kernel pairs, finite locally free projections and quotient equivalences are exactly those constructed above. If $\mathcal X$ is empty take $J=\varnothing$.
